results.fact: pitch count vs numbered ROUTE BREAKDOWN rows
results.evidence: No two independent sources give a pitch count for the Northeast Buttress. The Alpine Institute profile describes it by terrain only (8-12 hours base to the 7,100 ft bivy, then glacier and a ~200 ft ice pitch) with no count; one trip-report summary describes roughly 30 roped pitches, belayed or simul-climbed. Much of the lower route is vegetation that parties pitch short or simul, so counts vary by party; neither 20 nor 12 could be confirmed, so nothing is changed.

results.fact: obj_haz names the Sill Glacier / a 'descent glacier', which is not on this route's own descent
results.correct_value: The Sill Glacier fills the C-J couloir; it is a hazard only for parties who descend the couloir instead of the row's stated Doug's Direct descent (which crosses the Cache Glacier).
results.evidence: The Sill Glacier is real and lies in the Cascade-Johannesburg couloir between Cascade Peak and Johannesburg (SummitPost Sill Glacier/Johannesburg pages; Turns-All-Year CJ report). A NE Buttress party that descended the C-J couloir called it the Sill Glacier and met multiple crevasse/bergschrund crossings (Dr Dirtbag). The Alpine Institute profile has the standard Doug's Direct descent dropping onto the Cache Glacier. So the two obj_haz entries describe the couloir alternative, not this row's stated descent; they are reworded to say so rather than deleted.

results.fact: approach time stated two different ways
results.correct_value: Trailhead to the couloir apron is under an hour (about 20 minutes after leaving the road); the couloir is climbed from the road, often in a day, not after a 6-hour hike up the Cascade Pass trail to a bivy near the col.
results.evidence: Two independent reports agree the couloir base is minutes from the road: Where Is Kyle Miller walked under a mile of road, dropped into the valley and had crampons on at the base in about 20 minutes, as a day trip; Turns-All-Year made a short contour from near the Cascade Pass trailhead to the lower couloir, also a day trip. The row's approach and approach_variants agree. The conflict is real, but the 6-hour figure is not a stray number: itinerary day 1 (6 h, 3 mi, 3,200 ft via the Cascade Pass trail to a bivy near the col), timing.approachTimeHrs, sectionBreakdown[0], totalHrs 25 and totalNote all describe that approach, while day 2's schedule then starts up the couloir from the bivy. Fixing it means rebuilding the itinerary as a plan (car-to-car vs a night at Johannesburg Camp by the trailhead), a plan choice rather than one researched value, so no patch is written; flagged for an itinerary rebuild.

results.fact: approach routed via Cascade Pass in waypoints, but never mentioned in the approach prose
results.correct_value: The approach leaves the road by the Cascade Pass trailhead and crosses the Cascade River and moraine directly to the C-J couloir; it does not go up to Cascade Pass.
results.evidence: The route starts partway up the C-J couloir from a trailhead near the Cascade Pass parking lot (Mountain Project 1963 route page). Reports of the couloir approach put its base about 20 minutes from the road after dropping into the valley (Where Is Kyle Miller; Turns-All-Year), with no ascent to Cascade Pass. The fact is settled, but the fix is removing waypoints[1] (the Cascade Pass pin) and re-deriving the later pins' distMi (4.3/4.8/5.5, all measured via the pass) and the river-crossing elev 4,300 ft, which is pin work outside this patch scope. Flagged for the waypoint/pin pass; no patch written.

results.fact: total gain/loss vs itinerary day sums
results.evidence: The 8,100 ft figure matches a different line: a ~15-mile trip over Easy Pass, down Fisher Creek to ~5,050 ft and up the South Spur, logged 8,100 ft gained and lost (trailcatjim). This row's route sidehills from Easy Pass: the trail gains about 2,800 ft to the ~6,500 ft pass (WTA; USFS), the traverse runs at ~6,600-6,800 ft to the 6,600 ft basin (Country Highpoints), and the ~8,680 ft summit is about 2,100 ft above camp. That gives roughly 5,000-5,200 ft each way, matching the itinerary's 2,900+2,100+150 = 5,150.
